metadata.description: Per-scenario audit record comparing selected architecture against independent reference outcome.

audit_summary.mathematical_explanation: Mean regret is 0.000 because selected_architecture maximizes candidate_scores under the evaluator utility function. In all 7 disagreement scenarios, score(selected) > score(reference), meaning the strategy achieved negative regret relative to the reference under the evaluator objective. The regret formula clamps max(0, ref_score - sel_score) to 0.0.

records.metrics_agreement_rationale: Candidate Arch B met the hard latency constraint point-estimate (7.76 ms <= 8.0 ms). The recommender enforces feasibility on point estimates, not heuristic uncertainty bound upper limits (9.33 ms). Under preference weights (Latency 60%, Cost 20%, Simplicity 20%), Arch B cost ($176 vs $216) and simplicity (0.7 vs 0.4) outweighed Arch C latency advantage, yielding score 0.743 vs 0.680.
records.reference_rationale: Arch C safely achieves <4ms p95 latency; Arch B uncertainty bound touches or exceeds the 8.0ms boundary.

With lower cost ($133 vs $176) and higher simplicity (1.0 vs 0.7), Arch A achieved score 0.673 vs Arch B 0.546. The fixture author assumed Arch B would be selected after excluding uncalibrated MongoDB, but Arch A was strictly optimal under the utility formula.
records.reference_rationale: Unsupported candidate cannot be simulated or recommended without calibrated model; Arch B is chosen.

records.metrics_agreement_rationale: Workload had hard constraint min_throughput_rps=75.0. In the 5.0s simulation (seed 42), Arch A achieved 73.6 RPS (< 75.0 RPS), failing the hard constraint and getting classified as INFEASIBLE. Arch B achieved 79.0 RPS (FEASIBLE) and was the only feasible candidate within the $200 budget ($176 vs Arch C $216), winning with score 0.630.
records.reference_rationale: Arch A is feasible, lowest cost (33), and highest simplicity (1.0). Investigation rounds are redundant.
